notes.1a: Generally good marks here. The commonest mistakes were to classify manufacturing wages as a factory overhead and to include Sales in the manufacturing account.
notes.1b: Again, good marks in general. Errors included miscalculation of the reduction in the provision for doubtful debts and classifying income from rent as an expense.
notes.1c: Well presented by most candidates. Common errors were recording only one of the closing stocks, entering the wrong adjustments for the debtors figure and classifying the bank overdraft as a current asset.
notes.2i: correctly usually did well enough in (b)(ii).
notes.2c: Some good answers here, though some candidates discussed the various methods of depreciation which did not gain marks.
notes.3b: As the question gave the formula, most candidates gained full marks here, though some did not seem to understand the word Percentage (%) and gave the answer as 3.5:1 or 7/20.
notes.3c: Many correct answers here but almost half tried to use the formula of Fixed Costs divided by Unit Contribution, and as Unit Contribution was not available those candidates usually gained only one
notes.3e: Usually some marks scored here, though fewer gained full marks.
notes.3f: This was a good discriminator with many candidates giving the answer $469 000, as they saw a reduction in sales price as being synonymous with a reduction in sales quantity. ACCOUNTING
notes.general_comments: General Comments The mean mark was 17, with many candidates bunching in the middle range. Only a few candidates attained high or low marks. There were no relatively easy questions on the paper. Candidates were required to have some basic knowledge of accounting in order to answer any of the questions. The following questions prompted many correct responses: 1, 5, 8, 13, 17, 20 and 22. It is interesting to note that the management accounting questions do not have as high a correct response rate as the financial accounting questions.
